**Position Overview**
---------------------

* 12-Month Internship | Commencing February 2027 | Full Time | $58,893 +15.4% super

* Lucas Heights, Sutherland Shire Location / Bus from Sutherland Station

**About the Opportunity**
-------------------------

**A competitive edge over other Graduates!** Are you completing a degree in Science or Engineering and would like to gain valuable hands-on practical experience in your field? ANSTO's Year in Industry Internship program is your introduction to a career in nuclear science and technology at the home of Australia's most significant landmark and national infrastructure organisation.

**Be industry-ready!** The one-year program commences February 2027 and provides industry- based learning for students to apply theory and skills to the workplace and use this experience to enhance the value of their remaining study. You will get the opportunity to work with world- class, specialised scientific equipment to deliver on a range of industry and research projects. This opportunity is ideal for students studying one or more of the following degrees: .

* Chemistry
* Earth and environmental science
* Physics
* Forensic science
* Engineering
  

The internship is open to penultimate year students, and participants are required to defer their final year of study to work full-time. If selected for this opportunity you will need to provide a formal statement from your university confirming approval of your deferral of studies to participate in the program.

**About You**
-------------

*"This opportunity is ideal for someone with a strong technical foundation, proactive mindset, excellent collaborative skills and has a passion for science"* - **Isabella Naletilic, Radioanalytical Science Services Manager**

**Your Duties and Responsibilities**
------------------------------------

* experimental design and implementation
* maintenance, calibration and operation of laboratory equipment
* alpha, beta and gamma spectral analysis, including the maintenance, calibration, and operation of associated counting instrumentation
* radiochemical separations
* inorganic chemistry
* lead-210 dating of sediment
* laboratory housekeeping
* record keeping and data collation
* and more...

**About Us**
------------

ANSTO leverages great science to deliver big outcomes. We partner with scientists and engineers and apply new technologies to provide real-world benefits. Our work improves human health, saves lives, builds our industries and protects the environment. ANSTO is the home of Australia's most significant landmark and national infrastructure for research. Thousands of scientists from industry and academia benefit from gaining access to state-of-the-art instruments every year.

ANSTO's Nuclear Stewardship division maintains national nuclear science & technology capabilities and functions that are mandated by Government, regulators or otherwise considered essential to ongoing ANSTO operations. Capabilities include radionuclide metrology, measurement and monitoring of radioactivity in the environment, low and intermediate radioanalytical chemistry and nuclear forensics.

This position will be based in the Low Level Radioanalytical Group which maintains measurement capabilities to quantify naturally occurring radionuclides and difficult to measure radionuclides through alpha, beta and gamma measurement techniques, as well as lead-210 dating of sediments.

**Working with us you will enjoy**
----------------------------------

ANSTO employees are passionate about what they do. We enjoy being part of an organisation making a difference in the lives of Australians.

===========================

At ANSTO, we recognise that diverse teams deliver better outcomes. We are committed to creating an inclusive workplace where everyone can contribute and thrive.

We strongly encourage applications from:

* Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander peoples
* Women in STEM
* People with disability

----------------

All applications must be submitted through the online application system. Applications submitted via email will not be accepted.

For further technical information relating to this position please refer to the Position Description or contact Isabella Naletilic on (02) 9717 9187. For all other queries please contact Talent Acquisition on +61 **(02) 9717 9361.**

* The program is scheduled to commence in February 2027
* Opportunities are full-time paid placements
* Participants must defer their university studies for the duration of the program and provide confirmation from their university

**About Us**
------------

Lorikeet is redefining what customer support looks like — and we're just getting started.

We build AI that handles complex, high-volume support for fintechs, healthtechs, marketplaces, and delivery services. Not chatbot-tier AI. The kind that actually resolves tickets, gives support teams their time back, and raises the bar for what software can do.

We're backed by over $50M USD from QED, Blackbird, and Square Peg, with backing from operators like Claire Hughes Johnson (ex-Stripe COO) and Cristina Cordova (Linear COO), plus founders of Canva, Atlassian, and Airwallex. We're the first company since Canva to be funded at early stage by all three of Australia's top VC funds — which tells you something about the calibre of people who've looked closely at what we're building and said yes.

Our customers include some of the largest telehealth, fintech, and marketplace companies in the US and Australia — many handling over a million support tickets a year. The problems are real, the scale is real, and the work matters.

If you want to build something that genuinely changes how businesses and customers interact — this is the place.

**About the role**

Our Forward Deployed team works between our customers and our product. They take a customer’s whole support operation (the tickets, the systems, the policies) and turn it into AI agents that resolve real customer queries in production.

As an FDE intern, you’ll be part of that team from day one, not on a side project. The workflows you build will go live and handle real conversations for some of the largest fintech and healthtech companies in the US and Australia. You’ll have close support from the team and real ownership of the work you take on.

Day to day, you’ll:

* Dig into customers’ support tickets and data to find where AI can fully resolve queries, and where it can’t yet
* Build, test, and refine AI workflows from first draft through to production
* Help connect workflows to customer systems through APIs, and test integrations before they go live
* Join customer calls, share what you’ve found, and own defined parts of an implementation
* Use Claude Code and other AI tools to speed up analysis, build internal tooling, and improve how the team works

You’ll leave knowing how AI agents are deployed end to end at scale in regulated industries. You’ll also have hands-on skills in workflow design, API integrations, testing and evaluation, and LLM fundamentals, and experience turning a customer’s messy real-world problem into a working solution.

**We’d love to talk if you**

* Are curious and learn fast. You pick up new tools quickly and enjoy figuring things out.
* Are technically confident. You don’t need to be a software engineer, but you’re comfortable reading API docs and working with data.
* Sweat the details. You notice when something’s off, ask good questions, and follow through.
* Communicate clearly with technical and non-technical people alike.
* Are genuinely interested in AI. It’s a bonus if you’ve experimented with LLMs or built something with AI tools on your own.

**What's unique about this opportunity?**
-----------------------------------------

**A culture that's genuinely different.** Low ego, high trust, no tolerance for talented jerks. We work efficiently, keep hours flexible, and actually mean it — because life outside work matters. We're committed to building a diverse team and actively encourage applicants from underrepresented backgrounds. We care far more about user obsession and eagerness to learn than traditional credentials.

**A front-row seat to building something meaningful.** We're Series A and moving fast. You'll have real scope to shape the product and the company — not just execute someone else's vision.

**Performance recognized in real time, not on a calendar.** Promotions happen when you're ready — leadership meets every six weeks specifically to identify and recognize strong performers, so you're never waiting for an arbitrary review window to move up.

**We're AI-native, and we'll make you AI-native too.** Every person at Lorikeet uses AI in their day-to-day work (current favourite: Claude Code), with unrestricted access and no usage limits. You'll leave with skills that matter for the next decade of work.

**Twice a year, the whole company flies to Hawaii.** Headquartered in Sydney, with teams spanning the US and UK — which means getting everyone in the same place is something we invest in seriously. We spend the time hacking on ideas, building things together that wouldn't otherwise exist, and making memories that remind you why you joined a startup in the first place.

**A recruitment process built on respect, not hoops.** We keep it simple: a couple of informal chats to share our story and hear yours, followed by a paid ~two-day work trial. The work trial is genuinely the best part — you'll work on real problems alongside the actual team, get a true feel for how we operate, and we'll both come out of it knowing whether this is the right fit. No trick questions, no take-homes that disappear into a void. Just real work, done together.

If you're from an underrepresented background and don't tick every box, please reach out anyway. We know firsthand that diverse teams perform better, and we're proud that our team reflects a broad spectrum of identities and lived experiences.

**Our Commitment to Child Safety**

At KT OOSH, children’s safety, wellbeing and rights are our highest priority and underpin all decision making. We are a child safe organisation committed to the safety, participation and empowerment of all children.

We apply the paramountcy principle in all recruitment, employment and operational decisions, ensuring children’s safety, wellbeing and rights remain the primary consideration at all times.

Child safety responsibilities form an inherent and non-negotiable requirement of every role within our organisation. Suitability to work with children is assessed through recruitment screening, induction, supervision, performance development and ongoing employment.

We are seeking an educator who shares this commitment and demonstrates professional boundaries, respectful relationships and a willingness to act immediately when concerns arise.

**About the Role**

Do you love working with children aged 3 to 5 years and helping them build confidence, independence and school readiness through play-based learning?

KT OOSH is seeking a passionate, experienced and Diploma qualified **Pre K Team Leader** to lead our dedicated program for the youngest children attending our service in Rouse Hill.

At KT OOSH, our children have told us that what matters most to them is feeling welcomed, supported and having access to fun activities that match their age and interests. They value familiar educators who know them well, organise engaging experiences and support them throughout the session.

As our Pre K Team Leader, you will create a safe, welcoming and nurturing environment where children can develop friendships, explore their interests and feel confident participating in daily routines and play.

You will work alongside a supportive team of professionals who pride themselves on delivering high-quality education and care through engaging programs that reflect children’s interests, strengths and individual needs.

KT OOSH Services at IRPS and RHAC are operated by KT Services Pty Limited.

**Hours and Work Options**

We are looking for someone available for either of the following arrangements during the school term:

* **Approximately 32.75 hours per week**, working morning and afternoon shifts, Monday to Friday.
* **Afternoon shifts only, from 2:45 pm to 6:00 pm, Monday to Friday.**

**During vacation care, the role involves 6-hour shifts, either morning or afternoon, Monday to Friday.**

Please indicate your preferred term time arrangement and your availability for vacation care in your application.

**Key Responsibilities**

* Lead the Pre K group, keeping children’s safety, wellbeing, rights, inclusion and participation central to daily practice.
* Plan and deliver engaging, play based experiences aligned with the Early Years Learning Framework.
* Prepare welcoming spaces and age-appropriate activities that support children’s interests, confidence, independence and development.
* Build familiar, trusting relationships and support children through predictable routines and responsive interactions.
* Support school readiness through play, friendships, communication, emotional wellbeing and opportunities to practise everyday skills.
* Encourage children to express their views, participate in decisions and seek help from trusted adults.
* Maintain active supervision across indoor and outdoor environments, including during transitions and movement between spaces.
* Work closely with other educators to communicate supervision responsibilities and maintain appropriate coverage.
* Support daily routines, including sign in and sign out processes.
* Model positive interactions, professional boundaries and child safe behaviours, providing guidance to educators working within the group.
* Build respectful relationships with families and share information that supports each child’s participation and wellbeing.
* Maintain accurate records and contribute to planning, reflection and continuous improvement.
* Follow service policies, procedures, privacy requirements and expectations for the safe use of digital technologies.
* Identify and respond immediately to child safety, wellbeing or child protection concerns in line with reporting obligations.
* Support compliance with the National Quality Framework and service requirements.

**Qualifications and Experience**

Our ideal candidate will have:

* A **Diploma in Early Childhood Education and Care or an equivalent approved qualification**.
* Cert III working towards Diploma
* Experience working with children aged 3 to 5 years.
* Experience leading a group of children and supporting other educators.
* An understanding of play based learning and the Early Years Learning Framework.
* A warm, caring and professional approach.
* Strong organisation, communication and time management skills.
* Reliability and the ability to work collaboratively within a team.
* A demonstrated commitment to inclusion, diversity and respectful relationships.
* An understanding of child safe practices, mandatory reporting obligations and professional boundaries.
* A valid Working with Children Check clearance before commencing employment.
* A National Police Check.
* A Food Handlers Certificate or willingness to obtain one.
* Current First Aid, CPR, Anaphylaxis and Asthma certifications, which are highly regarded.

**Child Safe Recruitment and Employment**

As part of our commitment to child safety, applicants must:

* Participate in child safe recruitment screening, including qualification verification, Working with Children Check verification and referee checks.

Corporate legal, tax, trade and compliance teams are changing how they work as regulation grows and AI reshapes the job. Thomson Reuters™ helps them make decisions they can trust, with connected solutions that turn compliance into an advantage for the business.

  

This is a hands-on integrated campaigns and demand generation role. As part of TR's regional growth and demand team, you'll draw on global platforms and programs and adapt them to work for this region.

  

**Key Responsibilities**

In this opportunity as a Senior Demand Marketing Manager, Corporates AEM, you will:

  

* Build and run integrated Corporate and Compliance campaigns end to end: the idea and the offer, the content and channel mix, the build and launch, and the optimisation while they're live.

* Start from the customer and the regulator. Keep a calendar of the regulatory deadlines in each market, and use customer research, win and loss reviews, sales and partner conversations and engagement data to decide where, when and with what to be in market.

* Turn customer data, market insight and performance signals into relevant campaign decisions, ensuring audiences, messages, offers and journeys stay closely aligned to customer needs.

* Run always-on, full-funnel programs for each buying group, with ONESOURCE as the way in and a clear path to the rest of the connected suite.

* Test and learn with intent: set a hypothesis, read the results, scale what converts and stop what doesn't.

* Package each campaign as a campaign-in-a-box kit, with assets, audiences, journeys and a short playbook, so regional teams and partners can launch it quickly in every market, including co-branded versions partners run themselves.

* Work with regional marketing teams on campaigns for their markets, adapted to local buyers, languages, mandates and events, and bring TR's Synergy customer events into your programs.

* Partner with product marketing on propositions, proof and launches, and with content, performance marketing, account-based marketing and sales colleagues to bring each campaign to market.

* Localise TR’s global campaigns for the region, adapting message, proof, language and channels to each market and its mandates, with input from field marketing, so every campaign lands with local buyers rather than reading as a translation.

Own the Corporate and Compliance demand plan, budget and pipeline target, focused on winning new customers and selling new products to existing ones, and report sourced and influenced pipeline, direct and through partners, with conversion and cost per opportunity.

You’re a fit for the role of Senior Demand Marketing Manager, Corporates AEM, if you have the following required qualifications:

**About the Department**
------------------------

The Department of Industry, Science and Resources and our broader portfolio are integral to the Australian Government’s economic agenda. Our purpose is to help the government build a better future for all Australians through enabling a productive, resilient and sustainable economy, enriched by science and technology. We do this by:

* Growing innovative & competitive businesses, industries and regions
* Investing in science and technology
* Strengthening the resources sector.

The APS and the department offer a clear direction and meaningful work. You will be able to create positive impact in people’s lives whilst contributing to improved outcomes for Australia and our people.  
  
If you would like to feel a strong connection to your work and you are accountable, committed and open to change, join us in shaping Australia’s future.  
  
Please see the APSC’s APS Employee Value Proposition for more information on the benefits and value of employment within the APS.  

**About the team**
------------------

**The National Measurement Institute**  
  
We are the Australian Government’s national authority on measurement.  
  
At the National Measurement Institute (NMI), we empower innovation and protect trust in Australian industry and society through world-class measurement science. Join a team where your expertise drives national impact, your curiosity is nurtured, and the work you do creates trusted measurement for a fair, safe, healthy, and competitive Australia. Our employees enjoy career development opportunities, flexible working arrangements and the opportunity to shape Australia’s economic future through world-class measurement science.  
  
At NMI, precision meets purpose.  
  
We’re committed to building a diverse, inclusive, and impactful workplace by hiring people who share our values and bring integrity, collaboration, and innovation to everything they do.  
  
**Physical Metrology Branch**  
  
NMI’s Physical Metrology Branch provides Australia’s peak measurement standards for physical quantities. This enables measurements made in Australia to be accepted internationally, which is particularly important for trade. Our people share their expertise by providing measurement services from calibration and testing to technical advice and training. We contribute actively to international measurement forums and enhance our capabilities through research and development in line with national and international requirements.  
  
**Power Systems Technology Team**  
  
NMI's Power Systems Technology team develops advanced measurement technologies and delivers specialist testing and calibration services that support Australia's electricity network and clean energy transition. The team operates Australia's largest high-voltage and high-current laboratory and provides critical services to electric power utilities, equipment manufacturers and industry stakeholders. Supporting Australia's Net Zero ambitions, our work underpins the generation, storage, transmission and use of clean energy. Its capabilities span three key areas: high-voltage testing and calibration, calibration of power system voltage and current sensors, and the design and manufacture of highly accurate digital and analogue measurement systems.  
  
The team delivers more than 30 specialised testing and calibration services across a diverse range of power system equipment and measurement parameters. It also undertakes applied research in collaboration with universities, national metrology institutes and industry partners to develop innovative measurement techniques and technologies. Our team's experts contribute to the development of Australian and international standards through active participation in Standards Australia and the International Electrotechnical Commission (IEC). We provide technical leadership across a range of national and international working groups, helping shape the future of power system measurement science and engineering.

**The opportunity**
-------------------

This is a senior opportunity for an experienced electrical or power system engineer to apply their expertise to nationally significant infrastructure and measurement challenges. The role supports Australia’s high-voltage and high-current measurement capability, helping ensure that critical electricity infrastructure can be tested, calibrated and assessed with confidence.  
  
The Senior Electrical Scientist/Metrologist will work at the interface of practical power engineering, specialised measurement systems and national standards. The role involves leading or contributing to high-value testing and calibration services, capability development, applied research, stakeholder engagement, and representation in national and international technical forums.  
  
As the electricity sector evolves—with increasing renewable generation, high-voltage transmission, power electronics, grid-scale storage and emerging electrical infrastructure—the role offers the opportunity to shape measurement capability that is directly relevant to industry, regulators and the national electricity system.

**What’s in it for you?**
-------------------------

Join a community of professionals committed to technical measurement excellence and cutting-edge research. We invest in advanced facilities, foster collaboration with leading institutions, and support innovation in areas that include nanometrology, sports integrity, forensic analysis, cancer diagnostics, high voltage electricity, and clean energy. You will work with people who have diverse skill sets including scientists, engineers, policy specialists and regulatory professionals.  
  
You will build sought-after experience leading nationally significant high-voltage testing, calibration and capability development, while deepening your expertise in measurement science and national standards.  
  
As part of the Department of Industry, Science and Resources, employees at NMI are covered by an enterprise agreement and benefits include:

* Parental leave
* a vacation care subsidy
* $235 annual healthy lifestyle subsidy
* access to study assistance
* access to Employee Assistance Program - health, wellbeing, counselling and support when needed.

For candidates with highly specialised skills and experience, remuneration above the standard salary may be considered through an Individual Flexibility Arrangement (IFA), subject to delegate approval and departmental policy.

**Our ideal candidate**
-----------------------

* Leadership skills in a technical or scientific environment.
* Experience developing, operating or maintaining complex measurement, testing or calibration systems involving high-voltage and high-current applications.
* Strong analytical, problem-solving and innovation skills, including the ability to develop new measurement capabilities and improve existing test and calibration services.
* Demonstrated ability to build productive relationships with clients, regulators, standards bodies, industry stakeholders and scientific peers.
* Strong communication skills, including the ability to present technical information to a range of audiences and contribute to scientific publications, technical committees and professional forums.
* Demonstrated commitment to safe work practices, quality assurance and continuous improvement.

Additional qualities sought at the S&T8 level include:  

* Demonstrated leadership of scientific or technical teams, including mentoring and capability building.
* Experience developing strategic capability roadmaps, investment priorities and long-term technical programs.
* Demonstrated leadership and influence in technical forums related to national and international standards, accreditation or research.
* Recognition as a technical authority within a specialised field of measurement science or engineering.

**Qualifications**  

* Tertiary qualifications in Electrical Engineering, Physics or a closely related discipline.
* A postgraduate qualification or PhD in a relevant field would be highly regarded but is not essential.

*We’re looking for individuals who bring personal integrity and a sense of purpose, and who embody NMI values (Inclusive, Innovative, Accountable, Adaptable, Influential, and Strategic) while upholding the APS Code of Conduct. Our department has a commitment to inclusion and diversity, with an ambition of being the best possible place to work. This reflects the importance we place on our people and on creating a workplace culture where each and every one of us is valued and respected for our contribution. Our ideal candidate adds to this culture and our workplace in their own way. Even if you’re not sure you meet all the requirements, we’d love to hear from you!*

**What you will do**
--------------------

* Lead or contribute to the development, maintenance and improvement of Australia's national high-voltage and high-current measurement standards, reference systems, traceability chains, uncertainty analyses and specialist capabilities.
* Deliver and oversee complex testing, calibration and measurement services, applying expert technical knowledge to solve complex measurement challenges and provide authoritative advice to clients and stakeholders.
* Drive innovation, research and service development activities to address emerging measurement needs and support future capability requirements within Australia's electricity sector.
* Lead or contribute to strategic capability, workforce and infrastructure planning, while providing technical leadership, supervision and mentoring to scientific and technical staff.
* Ensure laboratory operations comply with ISO/IEC 17025 accreditation requirements, NMI quality systems, technical procedures and workplace health and safety obligations.
* Build and maintain productive stakeholder relationships and represent NMI and Australia in national and international technical committees, standards development activities, accreditation forums, conferences and industry events.

**Classification Expectations**

At the S&T7 level, the successful candidate will typically:  

* Lead complex technical projects with the potential and willingness to develop into a leading national authority in power systems testing and calibration.
* Provide specialist technical advice within their field of expertise.
* Supervise and develop staff, including mentoring early-career scientists.
* Contribute to strategic planning and future capability development.
* Build effective relationships with stakeholders and clients to achieve program outcomes.

*S&T8*  
  
At the S&T8 level, the successful candidate will in addition:  

* Provide strategic leadership for Australia's high-voltage and high-current measurement capability.
* Lead a team and allocate resources to achieve organisational objectives and national priorities.
* Influence technical directions, measurement strategies and standards development at a national and international level.
* Develop and implement long-term capability roadmaps and investment priorities.

**Job Description**

  

*This is a* *12-month fixed term contract role.*

  

As senior marketing manager, tax and accounting, you are accountable for marketing across TR’s Tax and Accounting Professionals (TAAP) portfolio in ANZ: Checkpoint, Checkpoint World and the ESG reporting solution. You own the marketing plan and lead its delivery: generating pipeline for a sales-led business, growing and retaining the customer base, and building the market presence of TR’s tax and accounting brands. The role is roughly 30% strategy and planning and 70% hands-on execution: you design the plan and set the standard for the portfolio, and do most of the work yourself.

  

The portfolio serves accountants and tax professionals across ANZ and, through Checkpoint World, international tax specialists in markets outside the US. Much of the growth opportunity sits with existing and lapsed customers, and with new sustainability reporting requirements that are creating demand for the ESG solution.

  
  

**Key Responsibilities**

  

In this opportunity as a Senior Marketing Manager, Tax and Accounting- ANZ, you will:

* **Own the TAAP marketing plan:** create and deliver the integrated marketing plan for the TAAP portfolio in ANZ, aligned to business targets and agreed with the TAAP leadership team, covering priorities, budget, calendar and measures.

* **Drive pipeline and revenue growth:** deliver marketing’s contribution to TAAP targets through qualified leads, sourced and influenced pipeline, and wins, across ANZ and the international markets served by Checkpoint World.

* **Plan and run integrated campaigns:** lead always-on and launch campaigns end to end across email and marketing automation, digital, webinars, events and content, building audiences with Marketing Operations and doing much of the execution yourself.

* **Lead go-to-market for launches:** translate global product positioning and assets into regional launch plans, sales tools and customer communications, so new products and capabilities reach the right audiences and sales are ready at launch.

* **Grow and retain the customer base:** develop marketing to existing and lapsed customers, covering adoption, upgrade, renewal and win-back, with Customer Growth and Retention, and turn customer results into proof for future campaigns.

* **Set the standard for content and copy:** own the quality and consistency of TAAP marketing content, writing and editing priority material, reviewing and challenging what the business produces, and directing writers, designers and agencies.

* **Manage the digital and web presence:** own TAAP content across TR’s websites and digital channels, so it reflects the strength of the portfolio’s content brands, stays current, and performs in search and conversion, working with TR’s web and digital teams.

* **Measure, report and improve:** track and report marketing performance against agreed targets, and use testing, data and customer insight to improve results over time.

* **Partner with sales and the business:** act as the marketing partner to the TAAP leadership team and sales, aligning on targets, lead management and follow-up, equipping sales with messaging and materials, and building marketing capability across the business.

  

**Required Qualifications**

You’re a fit for the role of Senior Marketing Manager, Tax and Accounting- ANZ, if you have the following required qualifications:

* **Marketing planning:** You have built a marketing plan for a business or portfolio from a low base, set the priorities and budget, and gained agreement from senior stakeholders.
* **Integrated campaigns:** You have planned and run integrated B2B campaigns yourself, targeting prospects and existing customers (including upgrade or win-back campaigns), that generated pipeline for a sales team and delivered measurable results.

* **Content and copy:** You are a strong writer and editor, with the judgement to improve weak content and to brief writers and designers to a high standard.
* **Marketing technology and digital:** You do the work yourself in marketing automation, CRM, web content management, and digital channels, rather than only briefing others.
* **Measurement:** You use data to track pipeline from lead to win and to decide what to scale, fix, or stop, including running simple tests.
* **Sales and stakeholder partnership:** You have the confidence to tell senior stakeholders when work is not good enough, and the credibility to work as a peer to sales without formal authority.

  

**Preferred Qualifications**

* Experience marketing to accountants, tax advisers or other professional services firms, and knowledge of the Australian tax and accounting market, its professional bodies and events.

* Familiarity with ESG or sustainability reporting.

* Experience running webinars and events that produced pipeline, with follow-up agreed with sales.

* Experience building audiences and working with marketing operations on data, lead routing and consent.

* Everyday use of AI tools for research, drafting and analysis, with care in checking the output.

------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Cochlear’s mission is to help people hear and be heard. As the global leader in implantable hearing solutions, Cochlear is dedicated to helping people with moderate to profound hearing loss experience a world full of sound. We aim to transform the way people understand and treat hearing loss and innovate to connect people with future technologies. Our employees tell us that the number one reason they enjoy working for Cochlear is the opportunity to make a difference to people’s lives. Learn and grow with us as we tackle the most complex challenges in helping more people to experience a lifetime of hearing.

**The Opportunity** .

  

**Help shape how implant and surgical innovation reaches customers across Asia Pacific**

We have an exciting opportunity for a Product Manager, Implants and Surgical APAC to join our regional marketing team and help shape the commercialisation of Cochlear’s implants and surgical innovation portfolio across Asia Pacific.

  

In this highly collaborative regional role, you’ll translate customer and surgeon insights into product and launch strategies, lead market-readiness activities and partner with local markets and global teams to bring new technologies to market. You’ll work across Cochlear’s implants and surgical portfolio, including enabling technologies supporting surgical planning, navigation and procedural efficiency.

  

You’ll take a lead role in creating and executing regional product marketing and commercialisation plans across APAC.

  

Working with Country Marketing and Product Managers, Global Marketing and cross-functional partners, you’ll help ensure new technologies are positioned effectively, markets are ready for launch, and learnings from adoption and customer experience are used to optimise future activity.

  

The scope spans markets including Australia and New Zealand, Japan, Korea, India, China and Asian Growth Markets, giving you the opportunity to contribute regional insights and influence global product development and strategy.

  

**What you’ll do**

* Develop regional commercialisation and launch plans, including product positioning, value propositions, commercial objectives and market activation.
* Lead APAC market-readiness and commercialisation activity for new implants, surgical technologies and workflow solutions.
* Develop a deep understanding of surgeon workflows, operating-room environments and product-choice drivers and translate those insights into portfolio strategy.
* Partner with country teams to develop launch execution plans that support growth and market-share objectives.
* Lead cross-functional launch activity across Marketing Communications, Clinical Education, Regulatory, Localisation, Supply Chain, Sales Excellence and Country Marketing.
* Monitor adoption, utilisation and customer-experience metrics after launch and use the insights to optimise product uptake.
* Develop strong relationships with local Product and Marketing Managers, professional customers and selected Key Opinion Leaders.
* Represent APAC needs and insights in discussions with Global Marketing and contribute to future product-pipeline development.
* Support portfolio lifecycle activities including demand forecasting, product communications, configurations and end-of-sale planning.
Help local teams effectively communicate product value through training, positioning, competitive insights and key selling messages.  

  

**About you**

You’ll bring a combination of product expertise, commercial thinking and cross-functional leadership. You’ll be comfortable working across markets and functions, turning customer and market insights into clear priorities and taking initiatives from strategy through execution.

  

We’re looking for:

* A graduate qualification in marketing, business, engineering or science.
* At least 5 years' experience in product management, product marketing or commercialisation within implantable medical devices, surgical technologies or healthcare technologies.
* Medical device or healthcare industry experience.
* Demonstrated experience leading cross-functional project teams.
* Strong communication, influencing and relationship-building capability.
* Strong project and time-management skills, with the ability to deliver outcomes across multiple stakeholders and priorities.
Willingness to travel, up to approximately 30% of the time.  

  

**It would be great if you also have**

* Experience engaging with surgeons and operating-room stakeholders.
* Experience working across Asia Pacific or in another multi-country regional role.
Additional Asian-language capability.  

  

**Why this role?**

This opportunity combines regional scope, customer insight, product strategy and hands-on commercialisation.

  

You’ll have the opportunity to build deep knowledge of the implants and surgical portfolio, understand the realities of surgeon workflows and local markets, and help influence how current and future technologies are brought to customers across APAC.
